concepts.name: Objective function and decision variables
concepts.summary: Identify the quantity to be maximized or minimized and the variables one is free to choose.

concepts.name: Constraints and feasible set
concepts.summary: Explain how equality and inequality constraints restrict choices and define the set of feasible points.

concepts.name: Minimization versus maximization
concepts.summary: Understand that maximizing f is equivalent to minimizing -f and that both share the same optimal points.

concepts.name: Local and global optima
concepts.summary: Distinguish a point that is best in its neighbourhood from one that is best over the entire feasible set.

concepts.name: Translating word problems into models
concepts.summary: Turn a verbal problem such as maximizing area with fixed perimeter into variables, an objective and constraints.

concepts.name: Optimal value versus optimal point
concepts.summary: Distinguish the best objective value from the input at which it is attained.

misconceptions.text: The optimal value of the objective and the point where it is attained are the same thing.
Maximization and minimization are completely different problems needing unrelated methods.
A local minimum is always the lowest value the function can take.

concepts.name: First-order optimality condition
concepts.summary: Find candidate unconstrained optima by solving that the gradient equals zero.

concepts.name: Second-order test with Hessian
concepts.summary: Classify stationary points as minima, maxima or saddles using the definiteness of the Hessian.

concepts.name: Constraint substitution
concepts.summary: Solve simple equality-constrained problems by eliminating a variable using the constraint.

concepts.name: Graphical solution of two-variable LP
concepts.summary: Sketch a polygonal feasible region and find the best vertex of a linear objective.

concepts.name: Gradient descent iteration
concepts.summary: Carry out update steps moving against the gradient with a chosen step size.

concepts.name: Existence of optima
concepts.summary: Recognize that continuous functions on closed bounded sets attain optima while others may not.

concepts.name: Optimization on closed intervals
concepts.summary: Find extrema of a function on a bounded domain by comparing interior critical points with boundary values.

misconceptions.text: Every point where the gradient is zero is a minimum.
Optima of a function on an interval always occur at critical points in the interior.
A positive step size always guarantees gradient descent decreases the objective.

concepts.name: Lagrange multipliers for equality constraints
concepts.summary: Set up and solve the Lagrangian stationarity system to find constrained extrema.

concepts.name: Geometric meaning of multipliers
concepts.summary: Explain that gradients of objective and constraint are parallel at optimum and the multiplier measures sensitivity of the optimal value.

concepts.name: KKT conditions
concepts.summary: Apply stationarity, primal and dual feasibility and complementary slackness to inequality-constrained problems.

concepts.name: Convex sets and functions
concepts.summary: Test convexity via definition, Hessian semidefiniteness or composition rules and analyse its consequences.

concepts.name: Standard form linear programs
concepts.summary: Convert LPs to standard form using slack, surplus and split variables.

concepts.name: Simplex method
concepts.summary: Move between basic feasible solutions via pivots until optimality.

concepts.name: Step size and convergence in gradient methods
concepts.summary: Analyse how step size, conditioning and line search affect convergence of gradient descent.

concepts.name: Newton's method for optimization
concepts.summary: Use Hessian-based steps and compare their cost and speed with gradient descent.

misconceptions.text: Lagrange multiplier conditions alone identify the global optimum, not just candidates.
In KKT conditions every inequality constraint must be active at the optimum.
The simplex method moves through the interior of the feasible region.

concepts.name: Convex optimization problem structure
concepts.summary: Recognize convex problems and exploit that local optima are global and KKT conditions are sufficient.

concepts.name: Lagrangian duality
concepts.summary: Construct the dual function and problem and relate dual bounds to the primal optimum.

concepts.name: Strong duality and constraint qualifications
concepts.summary: Judge when strong duality and KKT necessity hold, and when they fail.

concepts.name: LP duality and sensitivity
concepts.summary: Derive LP duals and interpret dual variables and complementary slackness for sensitivity analysis.

concepts.name: Convergence rate analysis
concepts.summary: Compare algorithms by convergence rates and the effect of conditioning of smooth strongly convex objectives.

concepts.name: Quasi-Newton and conjugate gradient
concepts.summary: Explain how these methods approximate curvature cheaply and when to choose them.

concepts.name: Penalty and barrier methods
concepts.summary: Convert constrained problems into sequences of unconstrained ones and understand interior-point ideas.

concepts.name: Stochastic gradient methods
concepts.summary: Evaluate trade-offs of noisy gradient estimates, step schedules and batch size on large-scale problems.

misconceptions.text: Strong duality holds for every optimization problem so the dual gap is always zero.
Newton-type methods are always better than gradient methods regardless of problem size.
Stochastic gradient descent converges with a constant step size to the exact minimizer.

concepts.name: Choosing a problem class and reformulating
concepts.summary: Design reformulations or relaxations that turn hard problems into tractable LP, QP, conic or convex forms.

concepts.name: Conic and semidefinite programming
concepts.summary: Evaluate when second-order cone and semidefinite models capture a problem and how duality extends to cones.

concepts.name: Nonconvex landscape analysis
concepts.summary: Assess how saddles, local minima and initialization affect algorithm guarantees in nonconvex problems.

concepts.name: Integer and combinatorial optimization
concepts.summary: Judge relaxation bounds, branching and cut strategies for discrete decision problems and their complexity.

concepts.name: Complexity lower bounds and acceleration
concepts.summary: Evaluate optimal first-order rates and when accelerated methods achieve them.

concepts.name: Proximal and splitting methods
concepts.summary: Design algorithms for nonsmooth composite objectives using proximal operators and operator splitting.

concepts.name: Robust and stochastic optimization
concepts.summary: Formulate models that handle uncertain data and justify the chosen uncertainty model and its tractable counterpart.

concepts.name: Algorithm and solver selection
concepts.summary: Choose and diagnose methods and solvers based on structure, scale, scaling and accuracy requirements.

misconceptions.text: Any nonconvex problem is intractable and gradient methods on it are useless.
Rounding the solution of an LP relaxation yields an optimal integer solution.
Robust optimization simply optimizes the average case over scenarios.
